humic acid has a negative influence on lanthanide sorption onto kaolinite.
the presence of humic acid in the ternary lanthanide–kaolinite–humic acid system has a negative impact on the retention of lanthanides on kaolinite.
the sorption of lanthanide and gadolinium ions on kaolinite is strongly influenced by humic acid.

the influence of humic acids on the sorption behavior and migration of heavy metals in clay minerals.
the influence of humic substances on the mobility of heavy metal ions.
the migration of heavy metals in clay formations.

the sorption behavior is dependent on pH, the concentration of lanthenides, the presence of humic acids, and the presence of competing cations.
humic acid can be an important factor in the migration of heavy metals in clay minerals.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the sorption of metal ions onto kaolinites is suppressed by humic acid.
the presence of humic acid in a binary system of metal ions and kaolinite can influence the sorption behavior in a positive or negative way, depending on the experimental conditions.
humic acid can influence the migration of heavy metals in clay formations by forming soluble complexes with the metals.
The main takeaway from our work is that

humic acid is able to compete with kaolinite for the lanthanide cations, and that the sorption of lanthanides onto kaolinite depends on the concentration and the pH of the solution, as well as on the presence of competing cations.
, in the presence of humic acid, sorption of lanthanide onto kaolinite can be significantly suppressed, especially at lower concentrations of lanthanide.

the presence of humic acid in the ternary lanthanide/kaolinite system can influence the retention of lanthanide on the mineral surface, depending on the experimental conditions, such as pH value, lanthanide concentration and concentration of competing ions, and thus the migration of the metal.
